clue.text: Steal nothing in S African player's wallet

parts.note: to pocket something is to take it dishonestly

indicators.note: nothing sits inside the player's name, so the zero goes within it

parts.note: a Bok, short for Springbok, is a South African rugby international
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone pinches nothing from a South African rugby player's wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside BOK. A Springbok is a member of South Africa's national rugby team, often shortened to Bok.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocketbook is a small case for money and cards, the American word for a purse or billfold.

clue.text: Made music using two tones around piano

indicators.note: the two-toned word goes around the piano letter

parts.note: pied means having two colours, like a magpie
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone played music using a pair of notes and a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tones' suggests musical notes, but it means colours: PIED is black-and-white.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe is to play a pipe or flute, so piped means played a tune.

clue.text: Called in sick with temperature, being dimly romantic

indicators.note: sick means the letters are unwell and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone phones in sick with a fever, hardly a romantic evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A candlelit dinner has low, soft lighting and is the classic romantic setting.

clue.text: Suffering alcoholic stage of ultimate destruction

indicators.note: suffering means the letters are in distress and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker at the final stage of self-ruin is suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Eschatological relates to theology of the end times, the final fate of the world.

clue.text: Builder's outside, less inclined to work deprived of large heater

indicators.note: outside picks the outer letters of the builder's word
deprived of means the large letter is taken away

parts.note: lazier means less willing to work

explanation.surface: A builder sits outside, too idle to work and missing a big heater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' gives BR from Builder; 'deprived of' takes L from LAZIER to leave AZIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazier is a metal container holding burning coal, used to keep people warm outdoors.

clue.text: It may be first spoken without much sound

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the spoken word goes around the noise

parts.note: oral means spoken
a din is a lot of loud noise

explanation.surface: Something said first is spoken quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it carries its old sense of 'outside', the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal numbers mark position in a series, such as first, second and third.

clue.text: Spot detailed product information

indicators.note: de-tailed: the word for spot loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: a speck is a small spot or mark

explanation.surface: A spot gives a detailed specification of a product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'thorough' but means cut off at the tail, so SPECK drops its K.
explanation.definitionFit: Spec is short for specification, the technical sheet of features listed for a manufactured item.

clue.text: Praise heathen having a change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart means the middle letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen

explanation.surface: A heathen converts and gives praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The central G of PAGAN is replaced with E.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean is a song or speech of triumphant praise or thanksgiving.

clue.text: Was amorous rotter eating Japanese food?

indicators.note: the rotter word eats, so contains, the food word

parts.note: a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man
noodles such as udon and soba are staples of Japanese cooking

explanation.surface: A scoundrel turns romantic over a Japanese meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a noodle is only one example of Japanese food.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle, so this is the past tense of romantic petting.

clue.text: Spontaneous bad pun — rubbish cracks made better

indicators.note: bad means the letters are spoilt, so rearranged
the rubbish word cracks, so breaks into, the made-better word

parts.note: remedied means put right, made better
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: An off-the-cuff awful pun gets improved by rubbish breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' looks like a second anagram signal after 'bad', but it is the fodder for cheap junk, which 'cracks' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpremeditated means not planned in advance, so done on impulse.

clue.text: Criticise then serve a remedy

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
an ace is a tennis serve the receiver cannot touch

explanation.surface: Someone finds fault, then dishes out a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure-all, a remedy for every ill.

clue.text: Waste a lot of time in US prison

parts.note: dung is animal waste

parts.words: a lot of time in US
parts.note: eon is the American spelling of aeon, a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone wastes years in an American jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in US' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition: it tells you to use the American spelling EON rather than AEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground cell for holding captives, such as one beneath a castle.

clue.text: Kid turning, runs away from alien one's spotted

indicators.note: turning means the word for a kid is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy or kid

indicators.note: the runs abbreviation is taken out of the alien word

parts.note: a Martian is an alien from Mars
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A child turns and flees from an alien that has just been sighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' looks like 'seen', but the definition is a spotty creature. 'turning' gives DAL; 'away from' removes R from MARTIAN to leave MATIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalmatian is a dog breed with a white coat covered in black spots.

clue.text: King performing party piece

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
an actor who is on is performing
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A king performs a party piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical composition or movement with a recurring main theme.

clue.text: Leaf disease initially increasing in volume?

indicators.note: in music notation the soft marking at the start gives way to the loud one, so the first letter changes from piano to forte

parts.note: polio is a viral disease of the nervous system

explanation.surface: A sickly leaf, its illness at first growing larger, as if in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: In musical scores P means piano (soft) and F means forte (loud), so the opening P getting louder becomes F.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a single sheet or leaf of a book or manuscript.

clue.text: Prevent break behind ring in sink

indicators.note: the ring and break pieces go within the sink word

parts.note: to fall is to sink or drop

indicators.note: behind means the break comes after the ring

parts.note: O is a ring because of its shape
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: Stop the break that's behind the ring in the sink.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to prevent something by acting first, getting in ahead of it.

clue.text: Person to copy European fashion in turn

indicators.note: the European letter and the fashion word go within the word for turn

parts.note: to roll is to turn over and over
a mode is a fashion or style

explanation.surface: A European fashion is turning someone into an icon to imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is someone whose behaviour others look up to and imitate.

clue.text: Where learning is based on natural illumination?

definitions.text: Where learning is based on natural illumination?

parts.words: Where learning is based on natural illumination?
parts.note: a school run in the daytime, read whimsically as one lit by daylight

explanation.surface: A school that relies on daylight for its lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a playful reading: a school for pupils who go home each evening, imagined as one working by daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: A day school is one where pupils attend by day and go home at night, unlike a boarding school.

clue.text: Reason sailor's back taking alcohol across isle

indicators.note: the other pieces stretch across the island letter, which therefore sits among them
back means the word for a sailor is read in reverse

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
someone on a drug is taking it
ale is an alcoholic drink
I is the abbreviation for island or isle

explanation.surface: A sailor goes back across an island carrying drink, and wants a reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal; 'taking' means being on drugs, and 'across' lays the pieces over the island letter so it sits within them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reason or justification for a decision.

clue.text: Calm a mathematician's mounting ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means the mathematician's name rises, read upwards

parts.note: Carl Friedrich Gauss was a great German mathematician
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A mathematician's growing elation is soothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reverses GAUSS to SSUAG.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to soothe or ease a feeling, such as calming fears.

clue.text: Upset, this person enters bars lonesome, empty and sad

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the whole thing is turned upside down
the speaker letter enters, goes into, the bars word

parts.note: a cage is a set of bars
the setter speaking of themselves is I

indicators.note: empty means the inner letters are removed, leaving the outside ones

explanation.surface: Upset, a lonely person walks into pubs feeling empty and sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs but is CAGE; 'enters' gives CAIGE, 'empty' gives LE from lonesome, and 'Upset' turns CAIGELE over.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac means mournful, in the style of an elegy, a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Wood dweller boring flyer, say

parts.note: a dry speech is dull or boring
a flyer is one kind of ad, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A forest creature turns out to be a tedious bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' pretends to be a bird, but it is a printed handbill, an example of an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph in Greek mythology, a spirit living in the forest.

clue.text: Muslim more cheerful suppressing hesitation

indicators.note: suppressing means the hesitation sound is held back, removed from the word

parts.note: sunnier means brighter, more cheerful
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A believer grows happier by stifling any hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunni is a member of the larger of the two main branches of Islam.

clue.text: Racket tip one breaks

indicators.note: the one letter breaks into the tip word

parts.note: the nose is the tip or front end of something, such as a plane
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A racket's tip snaps in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, a clamour.

clue.text: Caught in corrupt place? It's doubtful

indicators.note: the caught letter is placed within the jumbled letters
corrupt means the letters are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught in a crooked establishment is a dubious case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' gives SEPTICAL, and 'in' sets C within it; 'It's' is fodder, not a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sceptical describes someone who questions claims and has doubts about them.

clue.text: Dry bathroom walls in house for children

indicators.note: the bathroom word walls in, encloses, the dry letters

parts.note: loo is British slang for the toilet
TT means teetotal, so dry, not drinking

explanation.surface: A dry bathroom is built into a family house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is the British game housey-housey, or bingo, not a building; lotto is a children's version.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game like bingo played with picture or number cards, popular with children.

clue.text: Fighter plane operator repeatedly an associate of thieves

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was a famous boxer, a fighter

indicators.note: repeatedly says the airline letters appear twice

parts.note: BA is British Airways, an operator of planes

explanation.surface: A boxer, an airline twice over, and a thieves' crony make an odd line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is British Airways, the UK's national airline.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, Ali Baba discovers the cave of the forty thieves and is linked with them.

clue.text: Keen on new technology, storing right part for service

indicators.note: the word for keen on stores, or holds, the right letter

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A tech enthusiast stores the right component for a computer service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is a church service, not computer maintenance.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is a psalm or chant sung at the opening of a church Mass.

clue.text: Was lacking in veracity, primarily?

indicators.note: lacking means the opening letter of veracity is missing from the word

parts.note: lived is a sense of was, as in existed

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of veracity

explanation.surface: Someone told falsehoods, chiefly by being short of truth.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVED (was, existed) lacks V, the first letter of 'veracity'. The whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who told untruths was lacking in truthfulness, so the whole clue describes the past tense of fib.

clue.text: Cope abroad, maintaining car without air-conditioning fault

indicators.note: maintaining means the jumbled letters hold the car word inside them
abroad means the letters wander about, rearranged
the air-conditioning abbreviation is taken off the car

parts.note: a Cadillac is an American make of car

explanation.surface: Coping overseas while running a car without aircon is a failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' gives PECO; 'without' leaves CADILL, an unpronounceable fragment that 'maintaining' tucks inside. A Cadillac is a big American car.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a minor sin or small fault.
